title: Batch, flex, and priority processing tiers

opening.headline: Batch operations during nighttime should be categorized by processing priority based on how much delay can be tolerated, in order to handle core requests reliably and at low cost.
body: Even with the same model, the cost, latency, and reliability can vary depending on how requests are processed. Processing a task that can wait several hours as if it were a request that a user must immediately wait leads to unnecessary costs, while handling critical requests too loosely can result in instability during peak times.

In this class, we compare Flex—which bundles requests and processes them in batches, enabling asynchronous calls but potentially at the cost of performance—and the Priority series, which offers faster, more reliable processing at a premium price. We also practice making decisions about work prioritization by example, such as dividing tasks based on allowable delays.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can describe the characteristics of batch, Flex, and priority processing levels.
Can provide a basis for selecting a processing level appropriate for delay tolerance

screens.title: Nighttime bulk operations are cheap, core requests are guaranteed.
screens.lead: Consider reading these two types of tasks and think about what problems might arise if they are processed in the same way.

visual.alt: A diagram showing large-scale document classification during nighttime and daytime customer chatbot following different processing paths.
labels: Nighttime document classification, tens of thousands per day
Response in less than a few seconds

paragraphs: There are two distinct types of work involved in one service. One involves classifying hundreds of thousands of documents every night. The results are only needed by the next morning. The other involves a chatbot responding to customers who wait in front of the screen during the day, requiring a response within a few seconds.

If both are handled in the same way, one side is prioritized while the other is sacrificed. If nighttime classification is adjusted to match the chatbot's processing method, immediate response values are achieved for tasks that otherwise would require waiting. Conversely, if the chatbot is adjusted to match the nighttime classification method, customers will have to wait for a long time.
Priority level is a choice among cost, delay, and reliability. This course addresses how to treat scheduling, Flex, and Priority based on a single criterion: delay tolerance.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Does allowing for delay mean we can wait indefinitely? The choice depends on the unit—minutes, hours, or days.

screens.outro: First, let's recall how many tasks in my workflow can be waited upon.

screens.title: Consider the work ratio that allows for delay
screens.lead: When you select a type, the instructor's thought summary is displayed. Since you haven't entered or submitted an answer, take a moment to think about your own work first.

items.prompt: Do we need immediate results from evaluation execution or data preprocessing?
items.answer: Mostly not. Model evaluation, data augmentation, and preprocessing are tasks that people do not need to wait for immediately. OpenAI's documentation also lists evaluation and data augmentation as primary use cases for batching and Flex. These are among the earliest candidates to be downgraded in priority.

items.prompt: What about large-scale classification or embedding generation?
items.answer: It processes large volumes at once, where the results can be used later. By sending tasks bundled in batches, you gain both a 50% reduction and a high speed limit. The greater the volume, the greater the savings.

items.prompt: What about chat where the user waits in front of the screen?
items.answer: This is not an easy task to tolerate delays. Consider reviewing the Priority series if you need to maintain standard processing or if delays are critical during peak times. Moving this task to a batch process will degrade the user experience. Dividing work into delay-tolerant components is the core concept of this lesson.

screens.outro: First, let's verify company-by-company how the deployment API operates.

screens.title: Batch API: Receive grouped items later
screens.lead: Select each tab to review the conditions of the company-specific layout API. On the last tab, common user workflows across the three companies are summarized.

tabs.label: Gemini
tabs.body: The Gemini Batch API processes large requests asynchronously when immediate responses are not required, at half the cost of the standard plan. The target completion time is 24 hours, though most requests finish much sooner. When sending input files, each file can be up to 2GB in size. The request unit is nearly identical to the previous call structure, differing only in that it is now asynchronous.

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body: OpenAI Batch API processes asynchronous request batches at 50% lower cost and guarantees completion within 24 hours. A key feature is its significantly higher throughput beyond the standard rate limits, helping users send many requests quickly even when previously constrained by rate limits. Each batch can contain up to 50,000 items, with input files capped at 200MB, and up to 2,000 batches can be created per hour.

tabs.label: Claude
tabs.body: The Claude Message Batches API charges all usage at 50% of the standard API pricing. Each batch is limited to either 100,000 requests or 256MB, whichever is reached first. Most batches complete within one hour, but if they do not finish within 24 hours, they expire; therefore, long-generation tasks should be submitted within a 24-hour processing window. Fast mode is a feature for adjusting synchronous latency and does not apply to batches.

tabs.label: common flow
tabs.body: All three services follow the flow of bundling requests into files and submitting them, checking the job status, and then retrieving the results upon completion. Suitable use cases include evaluation execution, bulk classification, and content enhancement—tasks where the results are not immediately used. Since the timing of result receipt is uncertain, it is essential first to verify whether the side using the results can wait.

screens.outro: Next, we'll look at Flex, which reduces costs while maintaining asynchronous calls.

screens.title: Flex processing: Cheap synchronous calls
screens.lead: When an item is selected, a description expands. Check in sequence how Flex differs from layout and what it must accommodate.

items.title: Gemini Flex: service_tier to flex
items.body: If the service_tier is specified as flex in the request, it is processed at 50% lower cost than the standard rate. Instead, latency is variable and availability is best-effort. If this field is omitted, the standard tier is applied by default. This tier is suitable for workloads where latency can be tolerated.

items.title: OpenAI Flex: Slow and occasionally resource-constrained
items.body: OpenAI Flex processes Requests for Responses or Chat Completions at a lower cost when the service_tier is set to flex. However, responses may be slow and occasionally lead to resource exhaustion. It is best suited for low-priority tasks such as model evaluation, data augmentation, or asynchronous operations. Guidance is also provided to increase the client's timeout to mitigate long wait times.

items.title: Difference between Batch and Flex: Invocation method
items.body: Batching is an asynchronous approach that groups requests for submission and retrieves results later, whereas Flex uses synchronous calls similar to regular calls. Therefore, you can reuse the code structure without making major changes by simply altering the service_tier value. On the other hand, batching does not offer the same separate thread pool or guaranteed completion time guarantees.

items.title: Design consideration: absorbs delays and failures through retrying
items.body: Flex, being a low-cost tier that accepts delays and resource shortages, requires the calling side to absorb these costs. Therefore, it's essential to predefine strategies such as setting a sufficiently long timeout, retrying at regular intervals when resources are unavailable, and falling back to a standard tier for requests that ultimately fail. Otherwise, the cost of handling failures may exceed the cost savings achieved by using the low-cost tier.

screens.outro: Let's look at the comparison table for the Priority series and the four processing methods at the opposite end.

data.notes: Gemini Priority designates service_tier as priority, offering low latency and high reliability at a premium price. OpenAI Fast mode uses the same approach previously known as Priority processing, designating service_tier as either fast or priority. Claude Fast mode specifies speed as fast and runs the same model with a faster inference configuration, thus maintaining the same level of intelligence. The lower the latency tolerance, the cheaper the option; conversely, higher immediacy and reliability come at a higher cost.

screens.outro: Let's work through an example of assigning work to grade levels using a comparison matrix.

screens.title: Explanation of the judgment regarding moving tasks that do not require immediate response into batch processing
screens.lead: The instructor walks through the process of assigning priority levels to four tasks. Select an arrow to proceed step by step according to the judgment order.

steps.title: Task list
steps.body: Assume four tasks for a single service: nighttime document classification, weekly report generation, customer chatbot, and payment fraud detection alerts. Currently, all are being processed using standard workflows, and we need to reduce costs while maintaining stability for core requests.

steps.title: Step 1. Specify Delay Tolerance
steps.body: The time waiting for results per task is specified in three levels: tasks that take less than a minute, tasks that take several hours, and tasks that take up to a day. Nighttime classification and daily reports are specified as taking up to a day, while chatbot and fraud detection tasks are specified as taking less than a minute.

steps.title: Step 2. Selection of candidate batches
steps.body: Moves nightly classification and weekly reports to batch processing with results available within a day. This achieves a 50% reduction compared to standard operations, and bulk processing encounters fewer limits due to dedicated allocation. Groups are divided to ensure they do not exceed batch limits for the number of records or file size, and processing time limits are set for jobs that cannot be completed within 24 hours.

steps.title: Step 3. Flex Candidate Review
steps.body: Responses must be received immediately, but internal tools or evaluation tasks that can tolerate slower performance are candidates for Flex. Cost can be reduced by simply changing the service tier without altering the call structure. However, due to potential resource shortages and delays, timeouts and retry mechanisms must be designed.

steps.title: Step 4. Priority Candidate Review
steps.body: Customer chatbot and payment fraud detection alerts must not tolerate delays. Maintain performance above standard; if delays become problematic during peak times, review Priority tiers or reserved capacity. This is a decision to trade delay and reliability for additional costs.

steps.title: Step 5. Cost Calculation
steps.body: Assuming that 60% of total input costs come from overnight classification and weekday reports, multiplying the 60% allocation by a 50% reduction yields a total cost reduction of approximately 30%. The remaining 40% is maintained at standard levels, and since priority usage during peak times incurs additional costs, those incremental expenses are included in the final cost calculation. These figures are based on assumptions for illustrative purposes.

screens.outro: Summarize the key points at the final screen.

screens.title: Delay tolerance directly translates to cost savings potential.
screens.lead: This lesson's key points are summarized. Please review your answers to the questions posed in the problem presentation screen.

paragraphs: Batching reduces 50% by using asynchronous batching, Flex maintains synchronous calls at a lower cost by accepting latency and resource constraints, while the Priority series offers speed and reliability at a premium price. Regardless of the tier, the model's capabilities are identical—what differs is the processing approach.

Going back to the first question, allowing delay means you must specify whether it's on a per-second or per-day basis before a choice becomes feasible. Each task should have its own tolerance level and grade assigned, and the limits—such as quantity, size, or completion time—should vary according to the grade, which must be reflected in the design. It concludes that different tasks within the same service should have appropriate, distinct grades.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: The workload proportion and cost reduction calculation in the text are based on assumptions for illustrative purposes. Recalculate them using your actual delay allowances and pricing.

glossary.def: This approach bundles requests and processes them asynchronously, retrieving the results later. A typical reduction compared to the standard is 50%.
Instead of reducing cost, this is a motivation level for dynamic delays and best-effort availability of asynchronous calls.
This is a tier that offers priority processing and low latency at a premium price.
The limit of time that a task can wait to receive a result.

misconceptions.myth: Batching has no advantages except that it is slow.
misconceptions.fact: There is an additional advantage of a high limit, in addition to 50% savings. This is the most efficient option when it comes to subsequent required tasks.

misconceptions.myth: Flex and layout are the same.
misconceptions.fact: Flex is a synchronous call similar to a regular call, while batch processing uses an asynchronous approach that submits tasks in groups. They differ in terms of limit pooling and completion time guarantees.
It simply processes the same model faster and more reliably. Claude's documentation also states that fast mode does not alter intelligence or capabilities.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Delay tolerance directly translates to cost savings potential.
Batch and Flex accept delays and reduce costs, while Priority achieves speed and reliability at the cost of expense.
Processing is handled by separate priority levels per work unit.
Each grade has different limits and conditions, such as quantity, size, and completion time.
